title: Functions
summary: Reusable blocks of code with a name, parameters, and optional return values. Functions are values in Luau — you can store them in variables, tables, and pass them around.

syntax:
-- named (global) function
function greet(name)
    return "Hello, " .. name
end

-- local function (preferred)
local function add(a, b)
    return a + b
end

-- function as a value
local multiply = function(a, b) return a * b end

details.heading: Parameters and arguments
details.body: Missing arguments arrive as nil; extra arguments are ignored. A trailing `...` (varargs) captures any number of extra arguments.

details.heading: Return values
details.body: A function can return any number of values: `return a, b`. With no return (or bare `return`), calls produce nil. Returns only matter as the *last* expression in some contexts — `(f())` keeps just the first value.

details.heading: Method-call sugar
details.body: `obj:method(args)` is exactly `obj.method(obj, args)` — the object is passed as implicit first parameter `self`. That's how Roblox APIs like `event:Connect(fn)` work.

explanation.whatItIs: A function is a named recipe: give it ingredients (arguments), it runs the steps, and optionally hands something back (return values). Define once, call as many times as you like.
explanation.whyItExists: Without functions you'd copy-paste the same code everywhere. Functions give logic a name, a single home, and a contract.
whenToUse: Any code you write (or might use) twice
To name a chunk of logic so readers see intent: `giveReward(player)` instead of 12 inlined lines
whenNotToUse: Don't wrap a single obvious line just to look busy — though a *named* line is still often worth it for readability
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local function add(a, b)   -- the recipe
    return a + b
end

local result = add(2, 3)   -- the call
-- a=2, b=3 inside; result is now 5
```
Calling a function is handing over inputs and (maybe) receiving outputs.
tips: Prefer `local function` — same reasons as local variables
Return early for guards: `if not player then return end` keeps nesting shallow
Functions are values: you can put them in tables (command handlers) or return them from functions (factories)
commonMistakes: Calling before defining: `local function` must be declared before use
Forgetting `return`, so the caller gets nil
Confusing `print(f())` with `print(f)` — the second prints the function itself, not its result

examples.title: Defining and calling
examples.code:
local function applyDamage(target, amount)
    if not target or not target:FindFirstChild("Humanoid") then
        return false   -- guard: no humanoid, no damage
    end
    target.Humanoid:TakeDamage(amount)
    return true
end

local ok = applyDamage(character, 25)
if ok then print("Hit!") end
examples.whyItWorks: The guard clause exits early when the target is invalid, keeping the happy path un-nested.

examples.title: Multiple return values
examples.code:
local function splitName(fullName)
    local first, last = fullName:match("^(%S+)%s+(%S+)$")
    return first, last
end

local first, last = splitName("Ada Lovelace")
print(first, last)   --> Ada  Lovelace
